channel.title: NPR Topics: Education
channel.description: We've been to school. We know how education works. Right? In fact, many aspects of learning — in homes, at schools, at work and elsewhere — are evolving rapidly, along with our understanding of learning. Join us as we explore how learning happens.

item.title: Head Start got her out of homelessness. Trump proposal threatens that help for others
item.description: A Trump administration proposal would change access to Head Start for children experiencing homelessness and the kind of care they would receive if they do get in.

item.title: When students attend these colleges, taxpayers often pay. Here's why
item.description: Federal data shows many borrowers who aren't paying their loans went to private, for-profit colleges — schools that often market to low-income students and rely on federal financial aid for revenue.

item.title: The colleges where borrowers aren't repaying their student loans
item.description: Millions of federal student loan borrowers are in default or well on their way. New federal data shows that tens of thousands of them attended the same problematic schools.

item.title: In Florida, textbook publishers are minimizing or removing climate change coverage
item.description: The words "climate change" are slowly being removed from textbooks in Florida and from the state's education standards.

item.title: Special education head at Education Department abruptly resigns
item.description: The leader of the Education Department's special education office told employees she is resigning after less than four months in the role and as the agency overall is morphing and shrinking.
